name: Agreement with the Coeur d'Alene, February 7, 1894 (Harrison townsite), ratified August 15, 1894
promises: The tribe ceded a strip one mile wide along the north line of the reservation, from the east bank of the mouth of the Coeur d'Alene River to the east boundary, where the town of Harrison and settlers were located (28 Stat. 322).
The United States agreed to pay the tribe $15,000, per capita, on completion of the agreement (28 Stat. 322).
compensation: $15,000 under the agreement. The Supreme Court records the cession was compensated to the tribe and no one else (Idaho v. United States, 2001).
today: Idaho v. United States (2001) cites this cession, which took in part of the lake, as evidence that Congress treated the submerged lands within the reservation as tribal; the Court held the United States holds the submerged lands in trust for the tribe.
